title: Spot the phishing message
intro: Phishing is a fake message that pretends to come from someone you trust, like a game company, a bank or a friend.
It tries to make you click a link, hand over a password or hurry. Hurrying you is a big clue!
Clues to look for: rushing, asking for passwords or codes, prizes that sound too good to be true, and strange links or spelling.

game.prompt: Sort each message: does it look safe or suspicious?
game.practiceNotice: These are practice messages we made up for this game. They are not real.

items.text: URGENT! Your game account will be deleted in 1 hour. Send your password to keep it.
items.explain: Real companies never ask for your password, and rushing you is a trick.

items.text: Mom: I'm picking you up from the library at 4.
items.explain: A normal message from someone you know, asking for nothing secret. If anything feels off, you can always call and check.

items.text: Congratulations! You won 10,000 free coins! Click here and enter your username and password to claim them.
items.explain: A prize you never entered for, plus a request for your login, are big clues.

items.text: A friend you only know from a game: I sent you a code by mistake, can you send it back to me?
items.explain: A code is like a key. Someone asking for a code you received is trying to get into your account.

items.text: Class group: Tomorrow we're going on a trip. Bring a hat and water.
items.explain: A normal message from your class, with no links and no secret requests.

items.text: Your parcel is waiting! Pay a small delivery fee at the link to get it.
items.explain: A surprise payment with a link is a common trick. Ask a grown-up to check.

quiz.question: A message says: "Hurry! Do it now or you'll lose your account!" What do you do?
options: Stop and show a grown-up you trust
quiz.explain: Rushing you is a clue that it's a trick. Stop and ask a grown-up.

quiz.question: Who can you tell your password to?
options: A game company that asks by message
Nobody, except a parent when needed
quiz.explain: Passwords stay private. Real companies never ask for them in a message.

quiz.question: Which of these is a clue that a message is fake?
options: It asks for a code or a password
It's from your class group about a trip
quiz.explain: Asking for codes or passwords is one of the biggest phishing clues.

summary: If a message rushes you, offers a surprise prize, or asks for a password or code, stop and show a grown-up you trust.
